title: FLA import: CPicSwf (embedded SWF placement) silently skipped
description:
flash8-import.ts line 837 hits a console.warn and skips any display element of type CPicSwf. The binary parser in flash8-binary.ts (lines 885-886, 1857) reads the record but the editor model has no corresponding display-object type so the import drops them.

CPicSwf appears when a SWF is imported via File > Import into a Flash 8 FLA. While rare, it causes a silent data loss in FLA round-trip fidelity.

Fix: investigate what data CPicSwf carries (position/scale/linkage to external SWF), then either map it to an existing model type (e.g. VideoDisplayObject) or add a new one.

--- FINDINGS AND RESOLUTION ---

Investigation (task 0908, 2026-06-10): The binary parser (flash8-binary.ts readCPicSwf) only extracts the fixed header: CPicObjBase (schema+flags+children) + a symbolSchema byte + the 24-byte placement matrix. The variable-length tail (950-5500 bytes per instance: AS2 clip-event scripts, instance name, color transforms, source SWF filename) is skipped via skipToNextBoundary() and is not decoded.

Critically, there is NO library-symbol linkage identifier in the decoded data. CPicSwf represents an externally-imported SWF placed on stage; it does not reference a library symbol. This means:
- Mapping to SymbolInstance is not possible (requires symbolId)
- Mapping to VideoDisplayObject is not possible (requires videoItemId)
- Full support would require a new dedicated model type AND decoding the variable tail to extract the source SWF path/instance name.

Resolution: Improved the console.warn to include decomposed placement details (x, y, scaleX, scaleY, rotation) and a clear explanation that the source SWF filename and instance name are in the undecoded variable tail. Updated the existing test to match the new message format and added assertions for the matrix fields. Full support deferred until a real-world use case justifies the new model type.
